chapter: Sanger, Ben Black and carnival balls
title: Ben Black's band, Lebowski and Art Landry
summary: One answer covers the arrangerless Sanger band, pianist Lebowski, Ben Black losing his voice so DeDroit emceed, and Art Landry.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: He used to lick more people and get drunk. If you fool with him, he'd knock them down. And right here was the same type, about six foot straight old man, did his handball every morning, or played golf with me. He's the handsome man. Now he plays character parts, the most ugly parts. He looks like a big old fat sneaky sheriff or something like that. But he came here not long ago. When he phoned me, he was out on the driving range. He hit some balls after I went out to see him. I said, Ray, you're getting a little stout. He says, if I take the stomach off I don't get the part. I said, you compared yourself. He's like, stomach helps to get the part. He says, I'm not the leading man but I'm doing very well. There was a saxophone player, played a nice tone. He walked in there to stand up. He didn't know any of us. And he says, I would like to meet the arrangers. And we all started looking at one arrangers. He says, you don't have any arrangers? We didn't. We didn't have an arranger. We'd say let's play jazz and blues. And we'd play them and go on. I'd get up and take a chorus and friend and get up and take a chorus and the whole bag would come in on the last seat and the house would come down. We had the audience strained. They didn't have us strained. That's a fact. They just, and we had Lebowski up here. He was a wizard. Did you ever hear Lebowski? Only on record. He's great. His brother was a fine violinist too. Lebowski died early in life. He took $27,000 worth of insurance and about six months after they died. He went too long. But he must have had something wrong with his lawn. I liked him. He gave me a marvelous compliment on him when day is done. He was a good man. Oh, beautiful. And naturally when I bow I would point to Lebowski. He'd point to me, it's all you. You don't both would be hamming it up, you know. Well, that's for now. The first thing Ben Black told us, I'm very lenient. I'm not a great musician. I need your help. But I want you men to smile when a man's playing a solo as if he was your brother. Let all that petty hatred go up for tomorrow. When a man's taking off, he's great. Because if you don't reflect that he's great, the audience won't reflect it either. And in that band, 16 men, there were 16 jealousies. And they were all aimed at me. Because I was being paid the money. I was assisting the family. They didn't have the capability. When Ben Black got an iron giant and he couldn't talk, and somebody said, what about Johnny D. He'd write. Because I had been a leader all my life. I was just a side man that helped him work out that contract. And he said, Johnny, can you talk? I said, certainly. Am I talking? Can you announce the show? I said, surely. So I walk out and I say, ladies and gentlemen, due to the fact that Mr. Black has iron giant and can't speak, I've been asked to take over the show. The first act will be this. I didn't go into a long speech. First act will be Jones and Jones and something like that. Oh I'd say, so and so, I'd say, Singham. I said he was formerly with the Metropolitan Life Insurance Company. I'd get a laugh, you know. You know, a little carny joke and all that. Not too much. Don't make it long, see. Then if what Ben Black had picked out for the old show, I did a good wooden feature to me, I'd say, well Ben don't you think you ought to be down front with the horn? Because they're waiting all the time. When's he going to blow the horn? Yeah. So Ben says yes. Well I had to do that for Art Landry. You ever hear of Art Landry? Yes.
